2026-08-27 respell session: two genuine structural fixes closed 32 of the original 36 byte overshoot and dropped differing_halfwords from 180 to 163 (candidate_bytes 392 -> 360; wrong_instructions 142 -> 138). (1) The `prompt` buffer was rewritten from a raw `u8 prompt[12]` array (accessed as repeated `*(u16/u32*)(prompt+K)` casts) into `u8 prompt_buf[12]; u8 *prompt = prompt_buf;`, giving GCC one persistent base pointer to fold every field access into an immediate-offset load/store -- this alone dropped 392->368 bytes by eliminating four separately-materialized sub-pointers the old array-cast form produced (matching the reference's single `r7`-relative addressing for the whole struct). (2) The outer `for (;;) { BODY; if(c1) break; if(c2) break; if(c3&&c4) break; TAIL; }` loop was rewritten as `while (1) { ... }` with the exact same body -- this alone dropped 368->360 bytes by changing which loop-rotation layout GCC 2.96 chooses: `for(;;)` produced a checks-block-before-body layout requiring two extra unconditional branches (an entry skip-jump plus a backward continue-jump), while `while(1)` produces the reference's body-first/checks-after layout with a single backward branch at the very end and no entry skip. Confirmed via the raw compiler `.s` output (not just the packed `.insns` diff) that after fix (2) the control-flow shape (block order and every branch target) now matches the reference exactly; every remaining differing halfword is a pure register-allocation variance, not a structural one.

2026-08-27, remaining residual: the reference dedicates a 6th callee-saved-crossing value to caching `&0x03001e40` (the per-frame timer register) in r8 across the loop body's two separate reads of that address, and pays for it by spilling `frames` to `[sp,#0]` for its three per-iteration accesses (compare, increment-read, increment-write) instead of keeping it in a register. This candidate's compile makes the opposite choice: `frames` gets `fp` (fitting all 5 non-scratch cross-call values -- prompt/sprite/left/right/frames -- into the 5 available registers with none left over) and the `&0x03001e40` address is rematerialized from the literal pool at each of its two use sites instead of being cached, which is what costs the remaining ~4 bytes and the bulk of the 163 differing halfwords (they all cascade from this one swapped register assignment: sprite lands in r9 instead of fp, right lands in r8 instead of r9, etc). Tried and confirmed to have NO effect on this specific allocation choice, each verified by a fresh compile: an explicit `volatile u32 *hwReg` local (both loop-scoped and function-scoped) aliasing the two `0x03001e40` reads; swapping the declaration order and the statement order of `frames`/`sprite`; nesting the `frames > 15 && (...)` guard into two separate `if`s; typing `frames` as `u8`; swapping the `&&` operand order in the third break guard; folding `wave` into a nested block scope; expressing `render[0]`/`render[1]` as a two-field struct instead of array indexing; and initializing `frames` at its declaration instead of via a later assignment (this last one was strictly worse: 360 bytes but 166 differing halfwords). No source-level lever found in this session moved this specific register-allocation tradeoff toward the reference's choice; it may require either the true original source's exact expression shape (unknown, out of scope per CONTRIBUTING.md) or GCC-2.96-internals knowledge beyond what source restructuring alone can influence.
